checks.claim: Cells affect one another through activation, weights and rates even with independent conditional spike draws
checks.evidence: A spike adds1 to s_j by Eq7, hence changes input g_i by W_ij in Eq8, then changes rate by phi in Eq9. Later draws depend on this altered state. Conditional elementary independence does not imply full spike-train independence. This matches existing Poisson qualification at254.

checks.claim: Three-step ring update with Bernoulli spike indicator
checks.evidence: Main p6 reports stochastic Euler integration, dt.1ms, tau10ms, and per-neuron spike probability r_i dt. Display combines Euler decay s(1-h/tau) with unit event increment X_i. X is defined as0/1, so h*r is dimensionless; s is dimensionless activation. The stated small-rh condition is needed to approximate continuous Poisson events with at most one event per step. h/tau=.01 for reported settings. Footnote identifies display as guide notation assembling the reported method rather than copied source code. Aggregate population-count warning correctly limits this rule to ring implementation.

checks.claim: Track angle at rate maximum; average squared angular changes; compare with predicted diffusion and wrapped long-delay curve
checks.evidence: Main p6 explicitly measures theta from label of maximum instantaneous r, averages squared changes over trajectory, computes D/J from noise-free steady rate pattern and formulas, and uses periodic variance expression for Fig2D. Main p2 states quantitative match without free parameters for the illustrated networks. Main p3 caption identifies circles as simulation and solid curves as theory. Wrapped(-pi,pi) coordinate explains bounded long-time squared error; it does not restore initial angle. Approximate short-time linearity is correctly qualified.
